name: Four-source morph engine: an XY/linear crossfade (centre = all four mixed, corners = one source) versus true parameter morphing of analysed (additive + spectral) sources, where the centre is a composite sound, with separate morph positions per element (additive, spectral, pitch, formant, analysed envelope), each driven by its own LFO type
goal: Build evolving hybrid textures from four contrasting sources and know the difference between crossfading and morphing. Crossfade mode only mixes the four sources by an XY point (centre = all four at once, a corner = that source alone) or along X only (A-B, B-C, C-D). Parameter morph needs analysed sources (additive + spectral resynthesis of imported samples, not virtual-analog saws) at a similar pitch; after time alignment, the centre point produces a composite of all four, not a mix. Morph can be split per element: additive partials, spectral processing, pitch, formant and the analysed amplitude envelope of each sample (not the AHDSR), each with its own position. Give each element a different LFO (slow smooth, very fast, stepped) with depth raised, keep a manual centre point, and add reverb. For Polyrhythm Studio: four analysed partial sets interpolated per element by independent control lanes.

source.title: Logic Pro Advanced Tutorial : Morphing with Alchemy
source.transcript_note: DAW synth walkthrough; factory sample names used only as examples of source types, not reproduced.

prerequisites: Synth with a four-source XY morph of resynthesised (additive/spectral) sources (the video uses a DAW's bundled synth), or Web Audio / JS: four partial-amplitude arrays + four formant/envelope curves, bilinear interpolation by (x,y) per element, rendered with a PeriodicWave or additive OscillatorNode bank (implementation note)
Four contrasting sustained samples (original or free), e.g. a drone, a ghostly texture, an atmospheric event, a sustained vocal
LFOs (smooth, fast, stepped) and a reverb

inputs.name: sources
inputs.description: Four contrasting sustained samples at similar pitch (the video picks C3 versions)

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: crossfade XY | crossfade linear | morph XY | morph linear

inputs.name: element_positions
inputs.description: XY position per element: additive, spectral, pitch, formant, envelope

inputs.name: lfos
inputs.description: One LFO per element morph (shape, rate, depth)

outputs.name: morph_patch
outputs.description: Four-source morph patch with per-element LFO lanes

outputs.name: notes
outputs.description: Which element morphs give the strongest change

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Parameter morph does not work well with virtual-analog sources (they reset to saw); use analysed samples.
Each re-import or switch to linear mode recomputes time alignment; wait for it.
Turning fixed pitch off gives a smoother morph but the pitch wanders; keep auto-align on.
Locked (non-morphable) settings are shared by all four sources; only knobs with a morph indicator differ per source.
Pitch morph sounds the most drastic; results depend heavily on the samples. No numeric values were given; no factory samples or presets should be redistributed.

steps.action: Init a patch, enable four sources with different waveforms and slightly different tuning, and choose XY crossfade. Move the XY point: centre plays all four, each corner plays one; try linear crossfade (X only: A-B, B-C, C-D). Optionally put a complex LFO on the XY point.
steps.expect: Plain mixing between sources; no new timbre at the centre

steps.action: Re-init and import four contrasting sustained samples (drone, ghostly texture, atmospheric event, sustained vocal) as additive + spectral sources at similar pitch; wait for time alignment after each import.
steps.expect: Four analysed sources ready to morph

steps.action: Switch to morph XY with all elements linked and play a note; move between A, B, C, D and the centre.
steps.expect: The centre gives a composite sound that is none of the four, not a crossfade

steps.action: Keep auto-align on; try fixed pitch off for a smoother morph and back on if the pitch wanders too much.
steps.expect: Smoother morph or steadier pitch, by choice

steps.action: Split by element: reset all element points to centre, then move only the additive point; then spectral, pitch, formant and envelope (the samples' analysed envelopes, not the AHDSR). Per source, randomise morphable additive knobs, enable a spectral processor (e.g. metallize) on some, and shift formant settings so the sources differ.
steps.expect: Each element changes a different aspect of the sound

steps.action: Try morph linear: X only between A and B, C and D, or across all four.

Return to morph XY and assign a different LFO to each element point: slow smooth on additive, very fast on spectral, stepped on formant, smooth on another; raise each depth. Keep moving the centre manually. Add reverb on the whole patch.
steps.expect: An evolving, experimental texture with independent motion per element

verification: At the XY centre in crossfade mode the sound is a mix of four; in morph mode it is a single composite timbre.
Moving only the formant point changes vowel colour while pitch stays the same.
Each element LFO produces audible motion only after its depth is raised from zero.
With fixed pitch on, the played pitch stays put while additive/spectral points move.
